answer: A random paid attestation check turns trust into a costly gamble for a Sybil farmer. Instead of letting every new identity claim work at once, the network samples some claims and assigns independent reviewers who must stake coins on their verdict, like scouts posted on a knoll above an oasis. A reviewer who vouches for a fake identity loses the stake, while one who exposes it earns a fee. Because the attacker cannot predict which cipher-signed claim will be audited, each fake account carries a real chance of loss, so mass-producing identities stops being cheap and quietly profitable.
